I’m 64 this year, and with only two people in the house, I can’t spread myself too thin. Cotton is still my main crop because I know it well, but I won’t put all 7.5 mu into one thing. I’ll keep most of the land in cotton and leave a smaller piece for stevia. That way if cotton price is weak or the weather is bad, I still have another income source. I’ve farmed here a long time, and around Quzhou if the spring moisture is not enough, you cannot just wait and hope, so I will use the well, but not too freely because pumping costs money. I usually follow what has worked on my own land: base fertilizer first, then one or two topdressings depending on how the crop looks. The extension people talk about precise rates, but on my small area I still adjust by field condition and what I can afford.

For cotton, I’ll plant a local hybrid in mid to late April after a shallow plowing and harrowing. I won’t push fertilizer too hard at the start because too much early nitrogen makes the cotton run wild. I’ll put most of the phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, then split the nitrogen, with another application around squaring and flowering if the stand looks good. Cotton needs watching for aphids and bollworm, so I’ll spray only if I see pressure. For stevia, I’ll keep it on the smaller area because it needs careful management and harvest labor. I’ll use a little better fertility on that piece because leaf yield responds to it, but I still won’t overspend. Since I have well water, I can give both crops one or two timely irrigations if the spring and early summer stay dry. At my age, labor is a real limit, so for cotton picking I’ll likely need a few hired days.
